output.reason: Reported recurrent seasonal sneezing, itchy eyes and nasal stuffiness without any reported fever, breathing difficulty or unilateral symptoms can be managed with over-the-counter measures and guidance alone.
output.patientMessage: You can start today with an over-the-counter non-sedating antihistamine (such as cetirizine or loratadine) and/or a steroid nasal spray like fluticasone, plus saline rinses; nasal sprays take 1-2 weeks for full effect. Avoid decongestant sprays beyond 3 days. Message a clinician if symptoms don't improve in two weeks, and seek urgent care for wheezing, breathing trouble, face swelling, fever or one-sided blocked or bloody nose.
differential: Seasonal allergic rhinitis with allergic conjunctivitis
